short: A fast German battleship, Scharnhorst was an effective commerce raider until its sinking at the Battle of North Cape.
full:
Commissioned in 1939, Scharnhorst and its sister ship Gneisenau formed the core of Germany's surface raiding fleet early in World War II. Armed with 11-inch guns, the fast battleship sank the British aircraft carrier HMS Glorious in 1940 and inflicted heavy losses on Allied merchant shipping during Operation Berlin in 1941. In 1942, it participated in the famous "Channel Dash", successfully breaking through the English Channel back to Germany.

Relocated to Norway to threaten Arctic convoys, Scharnhorst sortied against Convoy JW 55B in December 1943. Intercepted by a much larger British force led by the battleship HMS Duke of York, Scharnhorst was cornered in the freezing darkness and battered into submission at the Battle of North Cape, sinking with only 36 survivors.
